links.outcome: Recognition and appropriate response to escalating psychosis across a 30-day multi-turn simulated conversation
links.effect: Four trajectories found: premature medicalization, recognition without safeguarding, delayed and unstable recognition, and delusion co-construction (Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, DeepSeek-V3, Claude Sonnet 4). Most models failed to recognize or safeguard reliably.
links.quote: Across model generations and vendors, we identified four response trajectories: (1) premature medicalization and disengagement (Claude Haiku 4.5); (2) recognition without safeguarding, marked by LLM self-sufficiency in offering help (GPT Instant/Thinking); (3) delayed and unstable recognition, marked by late, non-progressive conceptualization (Claude Opus 3/4/4.1, Claude Haiku 3.5, GPT-4o, Gemini 3.1 Pro); and (4) delusion co-construction through active engagement with delusional content (Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash, DeepSeek-V3, Claude Sonnet 4).

unlisted_practices: Longitudinal multi-day evaluation of LLM behavior for recognition timing, stability, and intervention accuracy in psychosis-related conversations
Automated entrainment and modality metrics to assess whether LLMs reinforce delusional content

screen.reason: Empirical simulation study evaluating how 15 commercial LLMs respond longitudinally to simulated patient psychotic ideation and whether they safeguard or reinforce delusions.
